<!-- pr-reviewer: e2e00bff98f5619de04618b7ab733e1b3367c665 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.**

This is a safety-tier review. The change sets the angle of Ramp descents that go to the posted G-code.

### What is good

- The default Ramp entry of Inside Contour, Circular and Bore does not follow a steep link angle now. This agrees with #1674.
- The Circular and Bore level transitions that the user sets to Ramp keep their link angle. The pin `explicit_ramp_transition_keeps_its_own_link_angle` shows this.
- The new suite has a provenance line and a gate map. The decision file `docs/decisions/1674-entry-ramp-angle.md` is present.
- The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1674`. The commit subject is conventional. No goldens, snapshot PNGs, process files, scripts, `.github/`, `build.rs` or dependencies change. No `crates/ui` code changes, thus no screenshots are necessary.
- No new `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` in production code.

### Local results (trial merge with upstream/main, clean)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | ok, 3 steps, 0 failed (kernel 159 s, motion 64 s, app 92 s) |
| motion lib | 343 passed, 5 ignored |
| `entry_ramp_angle` | 5 passed |
| `level_links` 12, `entry_approach` 9, `contour_inside_ramp` 2, `one_descent` 3 | all passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Mutations (done again by the reviewer)

1. Put back the old `contour_bore.rs` from main: `inside_contour_default_entry_ignores_steep_link_angle` goes RED (`entry at 4.755 degrees exceeds 3`). The other 4 pins stay green. Put back the fix: green.
2. Put back the old `descent.rs` from main: `circular_default_entry_...`, `bore_default_entry_...` and `explicit_ramp_transition_...` go RED (45 degrees). Put back the fix: green.

### Requested before merge

1. **`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_bore.rs:117` - an explicit Ramp level transition on Inside Contour loses its link angle.**
   `bore_entry` also runs for each level after the first (`contour_step.rs:105-106`, `first: false`). The arm there is the user's transition (`contour.rs:302`). The new line `let angle = crate::links::DEFAULT_RAMP_ANGLE;` applies to these transitions too. Thus a transition set to Ramp at 45 degrees now descends at 3 degrees. This is not what the PR body says ("Explicit level transitions keep their link angle"). Circular and Bore keep the link angle (`descent.rs:210`), so the operations do not agree now.
   I did a local probe (not pushed): Inside Contour, `Links { ramp_angle: 45.0, transition: Some(Entry3D::Ramp), approach.ramp_angle: 0.0, ..Links::PLANAR }`, level link Clearance.
   - upstream/main: entry 4.755 degrees, transitions 45.000 degrees.
   - this PR: entry 3.000 degrees, transitions 3.000 degrees.
   The 3 degree descent is not a gouge. But the operation ignores a value that the user set, and it does not tell the user.
   Possible fix (I tried it locally; all 5 `entry_ramp_angle` pins, `level_links`, `entry_approach`, `contour_inside_ramp`, `one_descent` and the probe pass):
   ```rust
   let angle = if !s.first && p.links.transition == Some(Entry3D::Ramp) {
       level_angle(p.links.ramp_angle) // this PR removes level_angle; keep it
   } else {
       crate::links::DEFAULT_RAMP_ANGLE
   };
   ```
   Note: `if s.first { DEFAULT } else { link angle }` alone is not sufficient. With no transition set, the later levels use the entry arm, and `inside_contour_default_entry_ignores_steep_link_angle` then goes RED at 45 degrees.
2. **`crates/motion/tests/entry_ramp_angle.rs:219` - add the Inside Contour case to the transition pin.** The pin uses only `circular_with_links`. Please add the same check for an Inside Contour with `transition: Some(Entry3D::Ramp)`, so that item 1 stays fixed.

### Notes (not blocking)

- `descent.rs:133` with `descent.rs:156`: a Helix level transition that falls back to a ramp now uses 3 degrees, not the link angle. The decision file records this, and it is the safer value. A shallower ramp can need more length, so more levels can go to the named plunge or a refusal. Please make sure that this is the intended result.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs:113`: the 3D ladder still uses `links.ramp_angle` for a default Ramp entry. This is the same coupling as #1674. If it is out of scope here, a follow-up issue (`P7`) can record it.
- The PR is a draft at the time of this review.
- Not run here: the full release gate and physical machining.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
